pages.summary: A control in a figure: a button, check box, text field, slider, list or menu, which calls back when used.
body: The Style chooses the control: `pushbutton`, `togglebutton`, `checkbox`, `radiobutton`, `edit`, `text`, `slider`, `listbox`, `popupmenu` or `frame`. Position [left bottom width height] is in the parent's Units (pixels unless set) from its lower left corner. String is its text (the items of a list), Value its state (a slider's position, a list's chosen item, a check box's 1 or 0), and Callback the function called when it is used, given the control and event data. `uicontrol(h)` gives a control the keyboard focus.

examples.title: A slider that sets a line's slope

pages.summary: Panels in a figure: a titled frame that holds controls and axes, and one whose buttons are chosen one at a time.
body: A panel groups what it holds, which is placed from the panel's lower left corner in its own Units, and moves and hides with it. A button group is a panel whose radio buttons and toggle buttons exclude each other: SelectedObject is the chosen one, and SelectionChangedFcn is called with the old and new choice when it changes.
syntax: p = uipanel('Title', title, 'Position', [left bottom width height])

examples.title: A plot and its settings side by side

pages.summary: A table of numbers, logical values or text in a figure, which can be typed in.
body: Data is a matrix, a cell array or a table; ColumnName and RowName label it, ColumnEditable says which columns take typing, and CellEditCallback is called with the indices and the old and new values when a cell changes.

examples.title: Three items, two columns to edit

pages.summary: Tabs in a figure, each holding its own controls and axes.
body: A tab group holds tabs, one shown at a time: SelectedTab is the one shown, and SelectionChangedFcn is called when someone picks another. Each tab is a container like a panel, its Title on the tab.

examples.title: Data and a plot on two tabs

pages.summary: Menus: in a figure's menu bar, and opened by a right-click on an object.
body: `uimenu` adds a menu to a figure's menu bar, or an item to a menu (an & before a letter underlines it; Accelerator a key that chooses it with Ctrl); its Callback (or MenuSelectedFcn) runs when it is chosen, and Checked, Enable and Separator change how it looks. `uicontextmenu` makes a menu that opens where someone right-clicks the objects whose UIContextMenu (ContextMenu) it is.

examples.title: A menu and a right-click menu

pages.summary: A toolbar in a figure, and its buttons: pressed once, or staying in and out.
body: A toolbar holds tools, each with a picture (CData, m-by-n-by-3 colours from 0 to 1, NaN showing through) and a tooltip. A push tool calls ClickedCallback when pressed; a toggle tool stays in or out (State 'on' or 'off'), calling OnCallback or OffCallback.

examples.title: Two tools with drawn pictures

pages.summary: The object whose callback is running and its figure, and the default way a figure closes.
body: Inside a callback, `gcbo` gives the object whose callback it is (and its figure), and `gcbf` the figure; outside one they are empty. `closereq` deletes the current figure: it is the default CloseRequestFcn, which a figure calls when its close button is pressed, and a function of one's own there can ask first.

examples.title: A button that names itself

pages.summary: A program waiting, with callbacks running, until a figure closes or something changes.
body: `uiwait` stops the program, while callbacks go on running, until the figure is closed or `uiresume` is called (from a callback), or for a time. `waitfor` waits until an object is deleted or one of its properties changes (to a value). Together with controls they make a program wait for its answer from a window.

examples.title: A program that waits for a button

pages.summary: Data kept with a figure or any graphics object, for its callbacks to share.
body: `guidata` keeps one value (usually a struct) with a figure, reachable from any object in it: a callback reads it with guidata(src), changes it and stores it again. `setappdata` keeps named values with any object, `getappdata` reads one (or all as a struct), `isappdata` asks whether one is there and `rmappdata` forgets it.

examples.title: A counter kept with a figure
examples.output:
ans =

     1

ans =

  1×2 logical array

   1   0

ans =

    'lab 3'

ans =

  logical

   0

pages.summary: Message windows: a message with an OK button, with an error, warning or information sign.
body: Each opens a small window and the program goes on at once; `uiwait(h)` waits until it is closed. `msgbox` can take a sign ('error', 'warn', 'help') or a picture of one's own, and `'modal'` last makes the rest of the page wait for it.

examples.title: A program that reports how a file went

pages.summary: Questions in windows: buttons, lines of text, a choice from a list, a choice among buttons.
body: Each waits for the answer. `questdlg` gives the text of the button pressed ('' when the window is closed), Yes, No and Cancel unless others are given; `inputdlg` the lines typed, as a cell array ({} when cancelled); `listdlg` the indices chosen and whether one was; `menu` the number of the button pressed (0 when closed).
syntax: answer = questdlg(question, title, b1, b2, default)

examples.title: A program that asks three ways

pages.summary: Choosing a file to open, a name to save under, a folder, or a colour, in a window.
body: `uigetfile` asks for a file among the page's files, by filters, and gives its name and folder (0 when cancelled; several with `'MultiSelect', 'on'`); `uiputfile` asks for a name and folder to save under; `uigetdir` for a folder; `uisetcolor` for a colour, as an RGB row.

examples.title: A program that opens a chosen file

pages.summary: A window with a bar showing how far a long job has come, and an empty window for a dialog of one's own.
body: `waitbar` opens a window with a bar and a message, and moves the bar (and changes the message) when called again with its handle; a Cancel button can be added whose callback marks the job to stop. `dialog` opens an empty modal window to fill with controls: until it is closed, the rest of the page takes no clicks.

examples.title: A bar moved on, and a dialog's style

pages.summary: A figure printed with the browser's printing.
body: Both open the browser's print window for the figure, where it can be printed or saved as a PDF.

examples.title: A program that prints its figure
examples.output:
function printIt()
f = figure; plot(peaks(20))
printdlg(f)
end

pages.summary: A function's help in the Help panel: its page, with examples and what they print and draw.
body: `doc` opens a function's page in the Help panel (or, alone, the list of every function by subject); `helpwin` opens it there too. `help` writes the short help in the Command Window instead.

examples.title: The short help, written out
examples.output:
hypot - sqrt(a.^2 + b.^2), without overflow or underflow on the way.

    c = hypot(a, b)

 How it works

    Python: elfun.py. numpy.hypot of the absolute values: sqrt(a.^2 + b.^2)
    without overflow or underflow in the squares.

 See also: sqrt, exp, nthroot, expm1, log

pages.summary: Timers: a callback run after a delay, and again as often as asked.
body: A timer runs its TimerFcn after StartDelay, once (`'singleShot'`) or every Period seconds (`'fixedRate'`, `'fixedSpacing'`, `'fixedDelay'`), TasksToExecute times or until stopped. `start` starts it, `stop` stops it, and `wait` waits until it stops. The callbacks run when the engine is idle, or at a running program's `drawnow` and `pause`. `timerfind` gives the timers there are (with given properties), `timerfindall` the hidden ones too.

examples.title: A timer made, and a program that counts down with one
examples.output:
ans =

    0.5000    3.0000

ans =

    'off'

ans =

     1


function countdown()
t = timer('Period', 1, 'ExecutionMode', 'fixedRate', 'TasksToExecute', 3, ...
    'TimerFcn', @(src, ~) disp(4 - src.TasksExecuted));
start(t)
wait(t)
delete(t)
end

pages.summary: A figure window moved on the desktop, and an object brought to the front or sent back.
body: `movegui` moves a figure's window to the middle of the desktop or to an edge or corner ('north', 'southeast' and so on). `uistack` changes the order in which an object is drawn among its siblings: to the top, up or down by steps, or to the bottom.

examples.title: A square brought in front of a circle
